analogy.title: The driver's seat principle
analogy.text: Aviation training begins in a cockpit, not in the passenger cabin. Day 1 of an OrchestrAI engagement is the cockpit. The Lead executes every command — the muscle memory acquired here is what enables debugging at 2 AM in production.

bullets: Day 1 — six manual installations and four AI prompts. The ratio is intentional.

Delegating installation now produces operational blindness later. This trade-off is non-negotiable in OrchestrAI engagements.

slides.title: Day 2 — First AI-Generated Code
slides.subtitle: Authentication. The feature with the highest client visibility.
slides.opening_hook: Authentication is the feature where AI-generated code most commonly fails. A precise prompt is essential to avoid shipping security vulnerabilities.
bullets: Authentication is the Day 2 priority — all subsequent features depend upon it.
We implement JWT-based authentication. Industry standard. Suitable for single-page applications.
The authentication prompt must include all eight intent components introduced in Module 3.
We will examine the actual prompt that produced the Issue Tracker's authentication — including the AI's first-pass deficiencies.

slides.title: The Authentication Prompt — All Eight Components
slides.subtitle: Production prompt · from the Issue Tracker engagement

hero_stat.label: intent components present — outcome, actor, validation, security, stack, acceptance, edge cases, data model

analogy.title: A locksmith's specification
analogy.text: A locksmith is not commissioned to 'build a door'. They are provided width, swing direction, lock type, key cuts, fire rating, and frame material. The authentication prompt operates by the same principle — every dimension explicit, or the product is incorrect.

bullets: OUTCOME — authenticated users access protected routes via valid JWT; unauthenticated requests receive 401.
ACTOR — three roles: Admin, Manager, Reporter — each with distinct menu visibility.
VALIDATION — email format, password minimum eight characters with mixed case, account lockout after five failed attempts.
SECURITY — bcrypt hashing at cost 12, JWT expiry 24 hours, refresh token rotation, server-side guards on every protected route.
STACK — NestJS @nestjs/jwt with Passport, Prisma User model, React Context for client-side authentication state.
ACCEPTANCE — successful login returns 200 with token; invalid credentials return 401; expired tokens trigger redirect to /login.
EDGE CASES — empty fields, malformed email, brute force attempts, token expiry during active session.
DATA MODEL — User entity: id, email UNIQUE, passwordHash, role ENUM, createdAt, lastLoginAt.
slides.memory_hook: Eight components. Each closes an ambiguity AI would otherwise resolve via assumption.
slides.closing_thread: We examine what the AI produced — and what required re-prompting.

slides.title: Manual Validation — Practitioner-Executed
slides.subtitle: Independent verification of AI output. Five steps. Approximately five minutes.
bullets: Step 1 — Execute npm run start:dev. Verify backend operation. Visit localhost:3000/auth/login; confirm 401 response.
Step 2 — Execute npm run dev. Verify frontend operation. Visit localhost:5173; confirm login page renders.
Step 3 — Submit incorrect credentials. Confirm error message display. Open browser dev tools — Network tab — confirm 401 response.
Step 4 — Submit valid admin credentials. Confirm redirect to dashboard. Confirm JWT presence in localStorage.
Step 5 — Issue curl request to /api/issues without authorisation header. Confirm 401 response. Server-side enforcement validated.
All five passing — authentication is considered shipped. Any failure — re-prompt with the specific error message.
slides.memory_hook: Five-step smoke test. Five minutes. This validation cannot be omitted.
slides.closing_thread: Authentication shipped. We proceed to the application shell.

slides.title: Re-Prompt That Resolved the N+1 Issue
slides.subtitle: Surgical · two sentences · references the specific file
bullets: Ineffective re-prompt — 'fix performance'. Vague; AI guesses. This approach should be avoided.
Effective re-prompt — 'In dashboard.service.ts, getDashboardMetrics() issues four separate Prisma calls. Combine into one query using groupBy with raw aggregations.'
AI response — a single Prisma $queryRaw with COUNT and SUM groupings; query count reduced from four to one.
Subsequent re-prompt — 'Add @@index([assigneeId, status]) and @@index([dueDate]) to schema.prisma.' Two re-prompts; complete.
Total elapsed time including re-prompts — approximately 90 minutes. From inception to shipped with indexes.
slides.memory_hook: Re-prompts must be surgical. Name the file. Name the function. Name the gap. Reference the shape of the fix.
slides.closing_thread: Authentication, shell, dashboard — all operational. The practitioner now experiences the result.
slides.narration: The re-prompt that resolved the N-plus-one. Ineffective — 'fix performance', vague. Effective — name the file, name the function, name the gap, suggest the fix shape. Two re-prompts, ninety minutes total, dashboard ships with indexes.

slides.title: Identify the gaps in this authentication prompt
slides.subtitle: Indicate each clause that violates the eight-component rule
slides.text: Add login to the app. Use JWT. Make sure the password is secure. Roles are admin and user. Block bad logins.

flaws.phrase: Make sure the password is secure
flaws.explanation: Imprecise. Secure by what mechanism? Bcrypt cost? Argon2? Length minimum? Complexity rules? Without specifying algorithm and parameters, AI will default to SHA-256 and ship a vulnerability.
Only two roles? The FDD specifies three — Admin, Manager, Reporter. Additionally, the action map is absent — who is permitted to perform what. Roles without permission scope are inoperative.
After how many attempts? With what cool-down? Account lockout? CAPTCHA? IP throttling? The term 'bad' has no defined shape — AI will ship a token check and consider the requirement satisfied.
